los.text: Perform a structured clinical examination of the hip.
los.html:
StepDetail
Look (standing)Gait (antalgic: short stance on the painful side; Trendelenburg: pelvis drops on the opposite side), posture, scars, wasting, leg length difference
Trendelenburg testStand on one leg: pelvis drops on the unsupported side = weak hip abductors on the standing side (superior gluteal nerve, OA, DDH)
Look (lying)Pelvis level, leg length: true (ASIS to medial malleolus) and apparent (umbilicus to medial malleolus)
FeelGreater trochanter tenderness (bursitis), temperature
MoveFlexion (~120°), internal rotation (~40°; lost early in OA), external rotation (~45°), abduction, adduction, extension (prone)
Thomas's testFlex the opposite hip fully: if the tested leg lifts off the couch = fixed flexion deformity
  • Finish: examine the knee and lumbar spine, neurovascular status; X-ray (AP pelvis and lateral hip).

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the knee with increasing confidence and accuracy.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Musculoskeletal › LO 7.
Accuracy tips
Compare with the other knee at every stage
Check for an effusion before stress tests
Lachman's is the most sensitive test for ACL rupture
Explain what each test shows

los.text: Demonstrate the correct technique for performing a digital rectal examination, ensuring patient dignity, safety, and effective communication throughout the procedure
los.html:
1Explain why and what it involves; consent; chaperone offered and documented.
2Position: left lateral, knees drawn up.
3. InspectSkin tags, haemorrhoids, fissures, fistulae, blood, warts, prolapse.
4Gloved, lubricated index finger; warn the patient; insert gently with the pad pressing posteriorly.
5. Assess
  • Anal tone (squeeze)
  • Mucosa all round (masses)
  • Prostate in men (size, surface, consistency, median sulcus; tender in prostatitis)
  • Stool and blood on the glove.
6Withdraw, inspect the glove, clean the patient, cover, thank, document (including chaperone).
  • Indications: rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, prostate symptoms, cauda equina (tone and sensation), constipation.

los.text: Take a history and explain a diagnosis
los.html:
History
  • Gout example: sudden
  • Very painful red hot swollen joint (often big toe, overnight)
  • Previous attacks
  • Risk factors (alcohol, red meat, seafood, sugary drinks, thiazide/loop diuretics, CKD, obesity)
  • Family history
  • Exclude septic arthritis (fever, unwell).
Explaining a diagnosis
  • What it is (urate crystals in the joint)
  • Why it happened
  • Treatment (NSAID or colchicine; allopurinol later to lower urate, not started during an attack in the first instance)
  • Lifestyle
  • When to seek help
  • Check understanding.
